techStack: Express 5.2.1, Zod 4.4.3, bcrypt 5.1.1 (native, not bcryptjs), better-sqlite3 12.11.1, jsonwebtoken 9.0.2, TypeScript 6, Vitest 4 + supertest
ESM project ('type': 'module' in package.json); verbatimModuleSyntax: true in tsconfig
TypeScript: target es2023, moduleResolution bundler, no strict: true but noUnusedLocals/noUnusedParameters enforced
bcrypt is async throughout: await bcrypt.hash(password, 10) and await bcrypt.compare(candidate, hash) — salt rounds 10
Zod 4 import: import { z } from 'zod'; schemas exported as named const with Schema suffix (e.g. registerSchema, loginSchema)
validate(schema) middleware calls schema.safeParse(req.body) and attaches result to req.validated; controllers read req.validated not req.body
JWT: jwt.sign({ userId, email, username }, secret, { expiresIn: '24h' }) sync; jwt.verify(token, secret) sync in requireJwt
Error handler responds { error, code, requestId } using err.statusCode/err.code for AppError instances; 500 for unknown errors
Test runner: Vitest with globals: true; setup file tests/setup.ts; supertest used for HTTP integration tests against live app instance
features: Existing routes: POST /api/auth/register, POST /api/auth/login, GET /api/auth/me (requireJwt), GET /api/products/*, GET/POST/DELETE /api/favourites/
GET /api/auth/me handler (authController.me) already uses req.user!.userId from JWT — never reads URL or query params — ownership already correct, no code fix needed for req 1
authService exports: register(email, username, password), login(email, password), getById(id: string): PublicUser|null — getById is synchronous
UserRow { id, email, username, password, created_at } and toPublicUser (strips password, maps created_at→createdAt) are private to authService.ts — userService must define its own equivalents
AppError(409, 'CONFLICT') is thrown by authService.register for duplicate email/username — same pattern should be reused for PATCH /api/users/me conflicts
Available errors: AppError(message, statusCode, code), ValidationError (400, VALIDATION_ERROR), AuthError (401, AUTH_ERROR); no ConflictError exists — use new AppError('...', 409, 'CONFLICT')
userProfile.test.ts tests PATCH /api/users/me (8 cases) and GET /api/auth/me ownership (1 case) — none of the PATCH infrastructure exists yet
architecture: Layer order: routes → (middleware stack: requireJwt, validate) → controllers → services → db/client
New files: src/schemas/userSchema.ts, src/services/userService.ts, src/controllers/userController.ts, src/routes/userRoutes.ts
Modified file: src/app.ts — add app.use('/api/users', userRoutes) following /api/<resource> mounting pattern
Routes wire middleware inline per-route: router.patch('/me', requireJwt, validate(updateUserSchema), updateMe)
Controllers: thin, async, read from req.validated (typed) and req.user, call service, respond or forward error via next(err) inside try/catch
Services: all DB via import { db } from '../db/client', db.prepare('...').get/run/all with positional ? placeholders — raw SQL, no ORM
Single SQL UPDATE with all changed columns in one db.prepare().run() call to satisfy atomicity requirement (req 12)
Uniqueness checks must use WHERE email = ? AND id != ? / WHERE username = ? AND id != ? to exclude current user's own row
edgeCases: Empty body {}: Zod refinement must reject any body where none of (username, email, currentPassword, newPassword) are present → 400
newPassword without currentPassword: Zod refinement enforces currentPassword must accompany newPassword → 400
Wrong currentPassword: throw error with message exactly 'Current password is incorrect' at status 400 (test checks res.body.error === 'Current password is incorrect')

Atomicity — multi-field conflict: test sends { username: 'renamed_before_conflict', email: <taken> }; after 409 response both username AND email must be unchanged — single UPDATE must not execute if any check fails
Uniqueness check must exclude current user's own row (WHERE id != userId) so submitting one's own unchanged email/username does not produce a 409
Password not in response: res.body.user.password must be undefined — checked at the nested res.body.user level (200 response wraps user as { user: { id, email, username, createdAt } })
Bcrypt hash verified by direct DB query using regex /^\$2[aby]?\$/ and asserting stored value !== plaintext new password string
Old password login after update must return 401 — test uses POST /api/auth/login as the oracle, not direct DB inspection
GET /api/auth/me ownership test passes ?id=<other>&userId=<other> — existing handler already ignores these, no code change needed
Rate limiter is vi.mocked in test setup — no changes needed to rate limiter middleware

tasks.requirement: 11 — Zod schema in src/schemas/userSchema.ts with optional username/email/currentPassword/newPassword and two refinements: at-least-one-field, and newPassword requires currentPassword
tasks.description: Create src/schemas/userSchema.ts. Export updateUserSchema as a z.object({ username: z.string().optional(), email: z.string().optional(), currentPassword: z.string().optional(), newPassword: z.string().optional() }) with two superRefine/refine calls: (a) reject if none of the four fields are present (enforces req 4 empty-body → 400), (b) reject if newPassword is present but currentPassword is absent (enforces req 5 → 400). Export the inferred TypeScript type as UpdateUserInput.

tasks.requirement: 12 — updateUser in src/services/userService.ts issues a single atomic SQL UPDATE; also satisfies reqs 6, 7, 8, 9, 10
tasks.description: Create src/services/userService.ts. Define private UserRow interface ({ id, email, username, password, created_at }) and toPublicUser helper (strips password, maps created_at→createdAt). Export async updateUser(userId: string, data: UpdateUserInput): Promise<PublicUser>. Steps: (1) if data.newPassword present, fetch row by id, await bcrypt.compare(data.currentPassword, row.password) — if false throw new AppError('Current password is incorrect', 400); (2) if data.email provided, SELECT 1 FROM users WHERE email = ? AND id != ? — if found throw new AppError('Email already in use', 409, 'CONFLICT'); (3) if data.username provided, SELECT 1 FROM users WHERE username = ? AND id != ? — if found throw new AppError('Username already in use', 409, 'CONFLICT'); (4) if data.newPassword provided, hash = await bcrypt.hash(data.newPassword, 10); (5) build a single UPDATE users SET <col>=?, ... WHERE id=? covering all provided fields (username, email, and/or password hash) and execute in one db.prepare().run() call; (6) fetch updated row and return toPublicUser(row).

tasks.requirement: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 — controller handler reads req.validated and req.user!.userId, calls updateUser, returns { user } with no password field
tasks.description: Create src/controllers/userController.ts. Export async function updateMe(req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction): reads userId from req.user!.userId and payload from req.validated (cast to UpdateUserInput). Wrap userService.updateUser(userId, payload) in try/catch — on success respond res.status(200).json({ user }) where user is the PublicUser returned by updateUser (which already has no password field); on error call next(err).
